items.title: Iran deploys naval mines in Strait of Hormuz, US intelligence says

featured_image.name: Iran begins mining Strait of Hormuz as Washington's tanker ...

items.description:
Iran has begun deploying naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes, according to U.S. intelligence, a dangerous escalation that threatens to deepen the blockade of the world's most critical energy corridor just as Washington's credibility on reopening it suffered a blow on Tuesday.

Small Iranian craft capable of carrying two to three mines each have been detected moving into the waterway, CBS News senior White House reporter Jennifer Jacobs reported on X, citing reporting by Jim LaPorta. While Iran's total mine stockpile is not publicly known, estimates over the years have ranged from roughly 2,000 to 6,000 naval mines of Iranian, Chinese, and Russian-made variants.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: US strikes Iran mine-laying vessels as escort claim collapses

featured_image.name: Iran-US tensions: What would blocking Strait of Hormuz mean for oil, LNG?

items.description:
The United States military is actively striking Iranian mine-laying vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff said on Tuesday, as the crisis over the world's most critical energy chokepoint deepened on the same day the US Energy Secretary was forced to delete a false claim about escorting a tanker through the waterway.

"CENTCOM continues today to hunt and strike mine-laying vessels and mine storage facilities," General Dan Caine told reporters on March 10, adding that the US had sunk or destroyed more than 50 Iranian naval ships in the first 10 days of the campaign, according to Reuters. The acknowledgment that Iran has mobilized mine-warfare assets into the strait marks a new and potentially lasting threat to a waterway that carries roughly 20 percent of the world's oil supply.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: New study finds no lab-origin signal for COVID-19 but flags 1977 flu

featured_image.name: Scientists discover key clue in pandemic viruses that reveal if they were made in a lab... including Covid and 'Russian flu'

items.description: A study published last week in the journal Cell offers researchers a new tool for one of the most contentious questions in modern science: how to tell whether a pandemic virus emerged from nature or from a laboratory. The research, led by evolutionary biologist Joel Wertheim at the University of California San Diego School of Medicine, analyzed seven major viral outbreaks from recent decades and found that most pandemic viruses show no signs of being pre-adapted for humans before their outbreaks — with one notable exception.[1][2]

items.title: Iran strikes Gulf desalination, energy sites as war widens

featured_image.name: ‘Reprehensible’: New wave of Iranian missiles, drones target Gulf nations

items.description: A widening war between Iran and a US-Israeli coalition has turned the Middle East's energy infrastructure into a battlefield, with both sides targeting oil facilities, tankers, and shipping routes in an escalation that has effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz and sent crude prices surging past $115 a barrel.

items.title: Nearly 700,000 displaced in Lebanon as Israeli strikes enter second week

featured_image.name: Thousands of people in south Lebanon flee intense Israeli ...

items.description: The death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon has reached 486, with 1,313 others injured since fighting erupted on March 2, Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health reported Monday. The escalation, now entering its second week, has displaced more than 667,000 people and drawn sharp international concern as Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called for direct negotiations with Israel to halt the violence.[1][2]

items.title: Ukraine says leaked Russian documents show 1.3M war losses

featured_image.name: Scale of Russian deaths in Ukraine signals trouble for Putin

items.description:
Ukraine's military intelligence has obtained classified Russian documents showing Moscow's own assessment of its battlefield losses at 1.315 million killed and seriously wounded since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced on March 10 following a briefing from intelligence chief Oleh Ivashchenko.[1][2]

"We have reason to believe that these figures are understated," Zelenskyy said in a post on X, adding that the documents also reveal a shifting casualty ratio: 62% of Russian losses are now deaths, with only 38% wounded.[1]

items.title: Trump and Netanyahu split over Iran war goals and timeline

featured_image.name: Benjamin Netanyahu to meet Donald Trump as Iran talks reach ...

items.description:
A widening gap between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the duration and objectives of the war with Iran came into sharp focus on Monday, as the two allies sent starkly different signals about how and when the conflict that began on February 28 should end.

In a phone call with CBS News on Monday, Trump said the war was "very complete, pretty much," and later told reporters the conflict would be "ended soon." But at a separate gathering with Republican lawmakers in Miami, he struck a more ambiguous tone: "We've won in ways, we haven't won enough." Hours later, Netanyahu's office released a statement in which the Israeli prime minister warned that Israel was "not done yet" with its offensive against Iran and vowed to continue strikes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Volkswagen to cut 50,000 jobs in Germany by 2030 as profit halves

featured_image.name: Volkswagen's sweeping cuts devastate workforce with layoffs ...

items.description:
Volkswagen announced Tuesday that it plans to eliminate around 50,000 jobs in Germany by the end of the decade, a sharp escalation of the automaker's restructuring efforts as annual profits fell to their lowest level since the 2016 diesel emissions scandal.

"In total, around 50,000 jobs are due to be cut by 2030 across the Volkswagen Group in Germany," CEO Oliver Blume wrote in a letter to shareholders included in the company's annual report. The company currently employs about 287,000 people in Germany.[1][2][3]

items.title: Tankers begin running Strait of Hormuz blockade as US backs $20B reinsurance plan

featured_image.name: Only a handful of ships risk Strait of Hormuz transit — who made it through  | News.az

items.description: A handful of oil tankers have begun running the gauntlet through the Strait of Hormuz, breaking an effective blockade that has choked one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints since the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28. The tentative resumption comes as the Trump administration rolls out a $20 billion government-backed reinsurance program and Iran issues new warnings to vessels attempting passage.

items.title: US Navy escorts oil tanker through Strait of Hormuz, Wright says

featured_image.name: US offers navy escort for oil tankers passing through Strait ...

items.description:
Energy Secretary Chris Wright announced on March 10 that the US Navy had successfully escorted an oil tanker through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first confirmed military-assisted transit since the waterway was effectively shut down by Iran's threats following the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran.[1]

Wright's announcement, posted on social media, offered few details about the operation and did not specify whether a broader escort program was now underway. The move comes after days of promises from President Trump and senior administration officials that the Navy would protect commercial shipping through the strait, which handles roughly 20% of the world's crude oil supply.[2][3][1]

items.title: ChatGPT launches interactive visuals for STEM learning

featured_image.name: What Teachers Should Know About ChatGPT's New Study Mode ...

items.description: OpenAI on Monday launched a set of interactive visual tools inside ChatGPT that allow users to manipulate mathematical and scientific formulas in real time, marking the company's most direct push yet to position the chatbot as a hands-on learning platform for STEM subjects.[1][2]

items.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic hits crisis low despite Western efforts to restart shipping

featured_image.name: Only a handful of ships risk Strait of Hormuz transit — who ...

items.description: Nearly two weeks after the U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran effectively shut down one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints, commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains at a near-standstill — though a handful of vessels have begun testing the waters under extraordinary risk, and a growing coalition of Western governments is working to reopen the waterway.

items.title: Aramco says it can restore output 'in days' once Hormuz reopens

featured_image.name: Aramco sees 'catastrophic consequences' for oil if shipping doesn't resume in Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Saudi Aramco warned Tuesday of "catastrophic consequences" for global oil markets if the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, even as CEO Amin Nasser said the company could ramp production back up "in days, not weeks" once shipping resumes through the vital waterway.[1][2]

Speaking on the company's fourth-quarter earnings call, Nasser said Aramco expects to reach the full 7-million-barrel-per-day capacity of its East-West pipeline within days, rerouting crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu to partially bypass the strait. The company also said its Ras Tanura complex — home to Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and a major offshore oil-loading terminal — was restarting after a precautionary shutdown following an Iranian drone attack last week.[1]

items.title: IEA calls for emergency oil reserve release at G7 meeting

featured_image.name: G7 holds off on tapping oil reserves amid Middle East war

items.description: The International Energy Agency called for a coordinated release of emergency oil reserves during a meeting with G7 finance ministers on Monday, marking a dramatic reversal from its position just days earlier that no such action was needed, as the war in Iran continues to choke off global energy supplies through the Persian Gulf.

items.title: Musk says X Money will enter early public access in April

featured_image.name: X taps William Shatner to give out invites to its payments service, X Money

items.description: Elon Musk announced on Tuesday that X Money, the digital payment system built into his social media platform X, will enter early public access next month. The confirmation, posted on X on March 10, marks the clearest timeline yet for a product central to Musk's long-stated ambition to transform the platform into an "everything app."[1][2][3]

items.title: Hegseth vows 'most intense' strikes yet as Iran war hits day 10

featured_image.name: Hegseth touts U.S. success in Iran war and takes questions on Operation  Epic Fury

items.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared Tuesday that Iran is "badly losing" as the United States prepared to unleash the heaviest bombardment yet in its 10-day-old campaign against the Islamic Republic, vowing that the day would bring "the most fighters, the most bombers, the most strikes" of Operation Epic Fury.[1][2]

Speaking at a Pentagon briefing alongside Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine, Hegseth said Iran's military capacity is deteriorating rapidly while its regional allies have abandoned it. "Iran stands alone and they are badly losing on day 10 of Operation Epic Fury," Hegseth said.[3]

items.title: Iran hits Israel, Gulf states as conflict enters 11th day

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Tehran vows to use powerful missiles, rejects Trump talks

items.description: Iran continued its barrage of drone and missile strikes against Israel and Gulf Arab nations on Monday and Tuesday, as the conflict triggered by the joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran entered its 11th day with no clear end in sight.

items.title: YouTube extends deepfake detection tool to politicians and journalists

featured_image.name: AI models spot deepfake images, but people catch fake videos

items.description:
YouTube announced Tuesday that it is opening its AI-powered likeness detection technology to a pilot group of government officials, political candidates, and journalists, giving public figures new tools to identify and report deepfake videos that use their faces without permission.[1][2]

The expansion marks the first time the platform has extended the tool beyond its creator community, where it launched last year for roughly 4 million members of the YouTube Partner Program.[3][1]

items.title: Iran war fuels global debate over shift to renewables

featured_image.name: Iran war threatens prolonged hit to global energy markets ...

items.description: As the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran enters its second week, the conflict's disruption of global energy markets is fueling a debate over whether soaring oil and gas prices could accelerate the world's transition to renewable energy. With oil having briefly surged past $100 a barrel and European natural gas prices spiking, leaders from the European Union to the United Nations are framing clean energy not just as a climate imperative but as a matter of national security.

items.title: Shots fired at US Consulate in Toronto as attacks on American posts spread

featured_image.name: U.S. consulate target of gunfire, no injuries reported: Toronto police |  CBC News

items.description: Gunshots were fired at the U.S. Consulate in downtown Toronto early Tuesday morning, Toronto police said, in the latest in a string of incidents targeting American diplomatic facilities amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.
